evidence.claim: 3Q26: 11 GW of gas equipment signed (8 GW SRAs, 3 GW orders), 13 GW of SRAs converted, 5 GW shipped; GW under contract 116 to 122; year-end target raised to at least 130 GW. 2032 slots are selling.
evidence.numbers: Signed GW fell from 20 GW in 2Q and missed BofA's 13 GW; the market had looked for 130-140 GW at year-end, so the new target is the bottom of that range. Backlog (64 GW) now exceeds SRAs (58 GW).

evidence.claim: Management: 3Q gas orders priced more than 20% above 4Q25 and FY26 price per kW about 50% above 2025; 'no change in our cash terms' for customers. Power segment EBITDA margin 21.4% vs a 17-18% guide.
evidence.numbers: The 'more than 20%' step-up vs 4Q25 is the same as stated for H1, so price is high and holding rather than still accelerating; 4Q price per kW guided lower on fewer aeroderivatives (call, single source).
evidence.source: GE Vernova 3Q26 call (Earnings Whispers transcript); release

evidence.claim: Aeroderivative orders: 57 units in 3Q26 vs 9 a year earlier, 127 in 9M26 vs 45; management says aero demand is strong but 4Q volume will be lighter than the 2Q-3Q run rate.
evidence.numbers: Only 13 aeros shipped in 3Q (39 in 9M), so the fast-to-deliver bridge units are being booked roughly 3x faster than they ship.

evidence.claim: Josh preview: gas prime genset lead times run into late 2028, with price escalators on distant orders; Cat Financial provided vendor financing on a 2 GW order.
evidence.source: Caterpillar 2Q26 call, via Josh CAT preview

evidence.claim: A 620 MW follow-on order of Jenbacher J624 gas engines (4.5 MW each, containerized prime power) from an unnamed US hyperscale developer, taking that customer to 1.72 GW.
evidence.numbers: Value and delivery dates not disclosed.

evidence.claim: Josh preview: heavy-duty frames mostly sold out through 2030 with new reservations four to five years out; 2H26 pricing at the high end of +10 to 20 points; BNP estimates about $790/kW heavy-duty and $1,800/kW aeroderivative.
evidence.numbers: Small buyers are pushed to aeroderivatives and engines.
evidence.source: GE Vernova 2Q26 call, via Josh GEV preview

evidence.claim: Record 3Q26: revenue $1,235.8mn (+138% YoY), product revenue above $1bn for the first time; FY26 revenue guide raised a third time to $4.4bn-$4.6bn. Management calls 5 GW of capacity 'just a milestone' and says backlog grows faster than revenue.
evidence.numbers: Cash did not follow: operating cash flow -$27.1mn and FCF -$180.6mn as contract assets rose $430.3mn; no backlog figure; RPO $661.2mn.

evidence.claim: SpaceX reached 1.4 GW of nameplate compute at Colossus on gas generation behind the meter, guided to over 2 GW by end-2026 and 'closer to 10 GW than 5' by end-2027, and targets 15-20 GW of power and cooling so that power, not chips, is the surplus. Mobile turbines (69 units) are being replaced by a permitted 1.2 GW plant, a 900 MW Solaris joint venture and 3.3 GWh of batteries.
evidence.numbers: Known generation supports about 2 GW; sites and power for the remaining 8 GW are not public. Q2 AI capex $15.8B.
evidence.source: SpaceX Q2 2026 call; World-Energy on the Mississippi turbine agreement

evidence.claim: New wording in the 3Q26 10-Q: leases not yet commenced now include 'energy-related infrastructure', and commitments include 'energy service agreements for data centers'. Neither appeared in the 2Q26 10-Q. Meta now contracts for dedicated energy as well as halls. It does not say whether this is behind the meter.
Trump posted that data centers are mandated to make their own electricity and should pay communities a dividend.
evidence.numbers: No executive action or thresholds; FERC this month rejected requiring bring-your-own generation in PJM, so words and rules diverge.

evidence.claim: SpaceX reported 1.7 GW of compute at 30 September, guided 2.2 GW by end-October and up to 3 GW by year-end, and aims to build 20 GW of incremental power and cooling ahead of about 10 GW more compute in 2027.
evidence.numbers: Capex $16.44B in Q3; Doosan has shipped the first of about five 380 MW H-class turbines reported for SpaceXAI.

evidence.claim: Lined up about 11.5 GW of gas power islands for up to 10 GW of AI compute; no customer yet.
Booked more than 1 GW of behind-the-meter gas generation for one data center.
Blackstone and others committed $5.34B for 49% of Williams' behind-the-meter power projects.
Off-grid power in Texas costs about $150–200 per MWh at about $2,700 per kW with up to 2x overbuild (Brian Janous).
Backlog hit a record $78bn (up about $38bn YoY); large gas prime engine orders now run to 2029 and turbines into 2030, and management says prime power demand 'continues to trend higher'.
evidence.numbers: Power Generation sales $3,421mn, +30% YoY; sales to users +75%. But adjusted margin ex tariff refunds was flat QoQ at about 20%: price is being absorbed by capacity costs, and the stock fell about 8% on an unchanged guide.
evidence.source: Caterpillar 3Q26 release and call (transcript, single source for backlog)

question: How fast are on-site and gas-to-compute builds scaling, and at what cost?
summary: On-site gas has gone mainstream and now has political cover: Trump says data centers must make their own power, INNIO took one developer to 1.72 GW of engines, and SpaceX plans 20 GW of its own power and cooling. Equipment is the bottleneck: heavy-duty turbines are sold out through 2030 and gensets run into late 2028, with prices rising. Costs remain high, about $150-200 per MWh off-grid in Texas, so it wins on speed, not price.
title: Behind-the-meter and gas-to-compute
